findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 2's ADR bullet (and the step 4 sentence), name `drift_refresh` and the reuse shortcuts as pipeline-only mechanisms that bear on re-review stability, and note that the cross-checks are inert by default. evidence: plan_review/__init__.py:542-543: "The three shortcuts below reuse or re-sign a PIPELINE attestation/verdict, so they fire only under the pipeline engine (ADR 0123)"

plan_review/__init__.py:557-561: "Progressive drift-refresh (Story 2): when the attestation is stale ONLY because reviewed code drifted (material + registry unchanged) and a cheap probe confirms the plan still matches, refresh instead of a full re-review", gated by `if engine == "pipeline" and sign ...`
Searching docs/adr/0123-selectable-plan-review-engine.md for 'reuse' returns no matches; the ADR has no pipeline-only statement for these shortcuts.
ADR 0052 §3: cross-checks are gated behind `verify.contradiction_xcheck_active` and `verify.comment_trail_xcheck_active`, "default `False`".
findings.finding: Step 2 says ADR 0052 §2's re-review stability 'is upheld by the drift floor and cross-checks, so it holds for the pipeline engine only'. That leaves out a mechanism that matters. The pipeline-only `orchestrator.drift_refresh` covers exactly the code-drifted, plan-unchanged re-review case, and the pipeline-only `reuse.idempotent_reuse`/`verdict_reuse` shortcuts are also skipped under agentic. ADR 0123 doesn't document any of these as pipeline-only either. Separately, both cross-checks are inert by default, so in default config they contribute nothing to pipeline stability. The amended ADR and doc would give an incomplete and partly overstated account of what upholds stability and of what the agentic engine skips.
findings.location: Plan step 2 and step 4 (ADR 0052 consequence sentence); Problem section's list of skipped steps
scenarios: An operator reading the amended ADR thinks enabling the drift floor plus cross-checks is all agentic would need to match pipeline stability, without seeing that agentic also never drift-refreshes or reuses a prior verdict.
A reader assumes the cross-checks protect default-config pipeline re-reviews when they are off.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite reason 1 in ADR 0123 §6. State that agentic findings carry no `citations`, so `drift_floor._finding_cited_paths` is empty and the drift floor would drop every novel agentic finding, even those citing drifted files. Keep the §3 point only as the operator decision, not as a logical override.
evidence: Plan: 'The drift floor and cross-checks remove findings from the blocking list, so running them on agentic verdicts would override that decision'

docs/adr/0123-selectable-plan-review-engine.md §3: 'Severity alone decides; a criterion's registry posture does not.' The mapping governs decision assignment, not whether a finding may later be removed.
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/agentic_verdict.py:33-49 map_finding: no 'citations' key on adapted findings
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/drift_floor.py:189-197 _finding_cited_paths reads finding.get('citations'); lines 259-265 drop when decide.drift_floor_drop is true
src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:122-148: a novel finding is dropped iff its citations do NOT intersect drifted_files, so an empty cited set always drops a novel finding
findings.finding: Reason 1 does not hold up, and it leaves out the strongest code-grounded reason. Dropping a blocker because the drift floor or a cross-check finds it novel-and-unrelated, contradicted, or already resolved does not reclassify its severity. So it does not 'override' the §3 mapping, which only says 'Severity alone decides; a criterion's registry posture does not.' The pipeline also runs its decide pass and then the tail removes findings. The fact that actually makes the drift floor unsafe on agentic verdicts goes unmentioned: agentic findings carry no `citations`. `agentic_verdict.map_finding` emits only finding, criteria, evidence, suggested_fix, severity, decision, tier and agentic_id. `drift_floor._finding_cited_paths` reads `finding['citations']` (kind == 'file'), so every agentic finding would get an empty cited set. `decide.drift_floor_drop` would then drop every novel agentic finding, including ones about the drifted code. That is exactly the drift detection the whole-HEAD trigger exists to keep.
findings.location: Plan step 1, first sub-bullet (reason 1: the drift floor and cross-checks 'would override that decision')
scenarios: A later reader or implementer weighs whether to enable the drift floor for agentic reviews. They see the §3-override argument, find it doesn't apply, and conclude the skip has no technical basis, missing that the floor would strip every novel agentic finding, including real drifted-code ones.
Someone later adds citations to agentic findings and assumes the ADR's reasoning still stands unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: In the §6 bullet, replace or lead reason 1 with: 'The drift floor keeps a novel finding only if its file citations intersect the drifted files (`decide.drift_floor_drop`). Agentic findings carry no `citations` (`agentic_verdict.map_finding`), so on an agentic verdict the floor would drop every novel finding, including genuine drifted-code findings, which defeats the guard the stale-head trigger exists for. The cross-checks and drift floor are also tuned to pipeline findings, and the operator chose (§3) that an agentic verdict blocks on the agent's blocker findings as reported.'

findings.finding: Reason 2 justifies skipping the rising and completion floors only as 'tuned to pipeline findings', which is vague when the code gives a concrete reason. The rising-floor drop predicate keys on per-finding `priority` (`decide.rising_floor_drop`: drop iff novelty >= t_novel and priority < floor). ADR 0123 §3 states that agentic findings carry no priority, so the floor's priority guard has nothing to evaluate on agentic findings.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the 'would override the 2026-11-09 decision' rationale with the actual reason: the 2026-11-13 operator direction itself, and/or a concrete technical incompatibility such as how `_recompute_verdict_after_drop` derives the verdict versus the agentic blocker-only rule.
evidence: "an agentic verdict blocks only on `blocker` findings ... The drift floor and cross-checks remove findings from the blocking list, so running them on agentic verdicts would override that decision"

Decision section: cross-checks "drop contradicted or already-resolved findings"; drift floor drops "a **novel** finding ... when its citations miss the drifted files" — neither concerns severity-to-bucket mapping
findings.finding: The first rationale in Step 1 does not follow. The 2026-11-09 decision says which severities make an agentic verdict block (only `blocker`). The drift floor and cross-checks drop individual findings (novel-and-uncited, contradicted, already-resolved), whatever their severity. Dropping a contradicted blocker does not make a major/minor/trivial finding block, so it cannot 'override that decision'. The ADR would record a rationale that does not support its conclusion.
scenarios: A future maintainer reads ADR 0123 §6, sees that the stated reason does not hold, and enables the tail for agentic thinking the constraint was a misunderstanding.
A reviewer of the amendment cannot tell whether the real reason is the operator's choice or a technical incompatibility.
